questions.scenario: A bank's mobile home screen currently makes seven REST calls on startup and is slow on 3G networks. Each screen needs a different combination of customer, account, card and transaction fields.
questions.question: Which approach addresses this most directly?
options: Adding more REST endpoints that each return everything
A GraphQL backend-for-frontend so the app fetches exactly the fields each screen needs in one request
Replacing REST with gRPC between the app and the backend
questions.explanation: GraphQL solves under- and over-fetching for client-driven screens. Browsers and mobile apps cannot call gRPC directly without extra infrastructure, and bigger REST payloads make over-fetching worse.

questions.scenario: After adding a GraphQL field recentTransactions on Account resolved with @SchemaMapping, SQL logs show one transaction query per account in every request.
questions.question: What is the standard fix in Spring for GraphQL?
options: Return all transactions in the Account type instead
Resolve the field with @BatchMapping (DataLoader) so transactions for all accounts are loaded in one query
questions.explanation: Per-parent resolvers cause the N+1 problem. Batch loading collects the parents and fetches the children in a single query.

questions.scenario: Card authorisation calls an internal fraud-scoring service on every payment and must respond in under 100 ms end to end. Both services are written in Java and owned by your bank.
questions.question: Which interface style fits this hot internal path best?
options: gRPC with Protocol Buffers and a short deadline on each call
questions.explanation: gRPC's binary format, HTTP/2 connections, strict contract and propagated deadlines make it well suited to low-latency internal calls.

questions.scenario: You need to remove the field middle_name = 4 from a protobuf message used by several services, and later add a new field preferred_name.
questions.question: What is the safe way to do this?
options: Reuse number 4 for preferred_name because the old field is gone
Rename middle_name to preferred_name and keep number 4
Renumber all remaining fields to close the gap
Delete the field and mark 4 as reserved; give preferred_name a new, unused field number
questions.explanation: Protobuf identifies fields by number. Reusing or renumbering corrupts data exchanged with older clients; reserving removed numbers prevents accidental reuse.

questions.scenario: A REST facade calls a gRPC account service with a 300 ms deadline. The gRPC call fails with DEADLINE_EXCEEDED.
questions.question: Which REST response should the facade return?
options: 504 Gateway Timeout as a Problem Details response
questions.explanation: DEADLINE_EXCEEDED means the upstream did not answer in time, which maps to 504. 404 would wrongly claim the account does not exist.

questions.scenario: You are preparing a GraphQL API for production.
questions.question: Which controls are important? (Choose two.)
options: Monitor the errors array in responses, not just HTTP status codes
Rely on CDN caching of POST /graphql responses
questions.explanation: Unbounded queries can overload the backend, and GraphQL errors usually arrive with status 200. CDNs do not cache POSTs, and a public GraphiQL invites schema exploration.

questions.scenario: A fintech must publish an API that hundreds of merchants, using many languages and frameworks, will integrate with.
questions.question: Which style is usually the best default?
questions.explanation: REST over HTTP with OpenAPI has the broadest tooling and the lowest barrier for external developers, and works with standard caches, gateways and security tools.
